title: Seller Sprint: Ingredients Deck (WIP)
body:
Slide 1 — Title: Seller Sprint: 'Ingredients' Deck (WIP)
Purpose: a lightweight, remixable mini-deck sellers can "cook" from during 1:1s and pilot conversations. Not a full playbook — a pantry of concise claims, proof, demo hooks, and micro-scripts.

Slide 2 — Intended audience & outcomes
- Audience: platform sellers, SEs running technical pilots, AE with engineer buyer
- Desired outcomes from using this deck: fast alignment on pilot scope, trigger Reserved/Dedicated conversation where appropriate, calibrate fallback economics early
- Timebox: 10–12 minute run for a discovery call, 4–6 slides to accompany a quick demo

Slide 3 — Core thesis (one-liner)
- Redwood helps teams turn uncertain LLM costs and latency into predictable product behavior by combining runtime routing, intelligent batching/caching, and dedicated capacity options.

Slide 4 — Five–ingredient checklist (the pantry)
- Ingredient 1: Latency SLO card — median vs p95 numbers for typical prompt sizes (30/150/512 tokens).
- Ingredient 2: Cost tradeoff badge — quick rule-of-thumb: when embeddings or small outputs dominate, prefer hosted; high-throughput token-heavy -> Dedicated.
- Ingredient 3: Fallback matrix — lightweight fallback options by severity: cheaper model variant, regional routing, cached prefix responses.
- Ingredient 4: Safety & compliance hooks — VPC/private deployment callouts, KMS integration, audit log examples.
- Ingredient 5: Pilot success metrics — latency SLO, token cost per 1k requests, error rate, and qualitative quality delta on canonical prompts.

Slide 5 — Microproofs & quick evidence (two-sentence bullets)
- Proof A (latency): Example customer reduced p95 latency by 24% after turning on prefix/KV caching + batching; ticket ref: JIRA-4581.
- Proof B (cost): E-comm search pilot cut per-query inference cost 37% after moving hot routes to Dedicated pool and enabling quantized variant.
- Proof C (reliability): Multi-region routing prevented a cross-AZ outage from affecting user-facing chat during a traffic spike.

Slide 6 — Demo hooks (30s verbiage + tech note)
- Hook 1: Live latency demo: run same prompt across hosted -> dedicated -> cached and show token/time metrics. Tech note: use sample prompt set on demo account, pre-warm KV cache.
- Hook 2: "Fallback flip" demo: simulate capacity drain and show automated routing to compatible cheaper variant. Tech note: show routing policy config in Console.

Slide 7 — Objection scripts (micro-scripts sellers can copy)
- Objection: "We can just host models ourselves cheaper."
  Script: "Totally — many customers start that route. The gap is predictable performance and the ops moat: we give you consistent p95 SLAs, automated fallbacks and per-route visibility you usually end up building for months. If you want, we can run a 4-week pilot comparing end-to-end costs and ops effort; we own the infra and runbooks while you measure ROI."
- Objection: "What about data security?"
  Script: "We support Private deployments (VPC + on-prem) and integrate with KMS/HSM. We can scope a short security checklist and run a technical call with SRE in the pilot window."

Slide 8 — Pilot blueprint (1-page checklist sellers can paste into emails)
- Duration: 4 weeks preferred (2-week quick proof possible)
- Goals: demonstrate stable p95 < target, per-query cost delta, and quality threshold on canonical tests
- Steps: 1) baseline measurement (1 day), 2) config + warm (3 days), 3) 2-week run under representative traffic, 4) analysis + handoff
- Required stakeholders: SE, Platform Eng (customer), Product contact (customer), Redwood SE
- Success sig: agreed metric gates + customer confirms acceptable quality on 80% of sample set

Slide 9 — Pricing angle (how to talk about economics in 90s)
- Key line: "We focus on unit economics, not just price per token." Show how batching, caching, and dedicated pools change the equation.
- Quick artifact: chart (placeholder) comparing per-1k-token cost across hosted default vs hosted with caching vs Dedicated with quantized model.

Slide 10 — Rapid-play scripts for different buyer personas
- Platform Engineer (focus): emphasize deterministic throughput and rollout controls, show Console route-level tracing.
- ML Engineer (focus): emphasize model variants, quantization advice, and eval gating in Redwood Optimize.
- Product Manager (focus): emphasize UX impact from latency improvements and predictable cost forecasts for roadmap planning.

Slide 11 — Unresolved questions / things to validate in sprint
- Confirm top 3 canonical prompts from the prospect (owner: SE)
- Decide pilot SLAs (p95 target) and acceptable quality delta (owner: AE + PM)
- Confirm whether logs can be exported into customer analytics pipeline during pilot (owner: SE + infra)

Slide 12 — Action items (next 72 hours)
- Claire: assemble demo account with sample KV cache + routing policy snapshot (due 2025-03-21)
- Aisha: draft pilot email template using the blueprint (due 2025-03-20)
- Miguel: prepare quick chart comparing per-token economics for small/medium/large outputs (due 2025-03-22)

Appendix — Speaker notes & quick links
- Link: Confluence page for pilot checklist: confluence:GTMSprint/ingredients-2025
- Link: Demo account dashboard: (internal) /dashboards/demo-pantry
- Reminder: this is intentionally modular. Pick 3–5 slides tailored to the buyer; avoid handing the whole deck in first email.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep claims short; sellers prefer copy-paste lines.
- Add a one-slide cheat for procurement negotiation: reserved capacity commitment language and negotiation levers (credits, ramp windows).
- Fetch a real customer example for the cost proof (look up JIRA-4789 and JIRA-4581).

Draft history and context
- Origin: distilled from SE sprint (Feb 2025) where field asked for a micro-deck they could remix on the fly.
- This draft intended to be converted into a 4-slide quickflip + 1-pager cheat for Slack snippets.

Feedback requested
- Which 3 micro-proofs feel strongest? (Aisha)
- Any legal language we should redact before field sharing? (Legal review request)

End of deck (WIP)
